comments:
So, is systemctl actually installed in $PATH? Where precisely? Does your distro play any games with paths?

Is this reproducible on a less hacky distro? i.e. fedora, debian, ubuntu or so?

At least on my system it is not.

This smells a lot like a broken local install, where systemctl wasn't properly installed.

~~Hmm, I cannot reproduce this with `initrd-cleanup.service`~~, but networkd with the following drop-in fails:
```
# /etc/systemd/system/systemd-networkd.service.d/override.conf
[Service]
ExecStart=
ExecStart=valgrind --leak-check=full /var/build/systemd-networkd
ExecReload=
ExecReload=/var/build/networkctl reload
MemoryDenyWriteExecute=no
PrivateTmp=yes
Environment=SYSTEMD_LOG_LEVEL=debug SYSTEMD_MEMPOOL=0
Restart=no
```
```
$ systemd-analyze verify systemd-networkd.service
/usr/lib/systemd/system/smartd.service:10: Standard output type syslog is obsolete, automatically updating to journal. Please update your unit file, and consider removing the setting altogether.
/usr/lib/systemd/system/mcelog.service:8: Standard output type syslog is obsolete, automatically updating to journal. Please update your unit file, and consider removing the setting altogether.
/usr/lib/systemd/system/alsa-restore.service:15: Standard output type syslog is obsolete, automatically updating to journal. Please update your unit file, and consider removing the setting altogether.
systemd-networkd.service: Command valgrind is not executable: No such file or directory
```
```
$ which valgrind
/usr/bin/valgrind
```
Ah, if a command is relative, then it fails.

review_comments: hmm, this appends the dash even if the provided path already had one, in which case it basically does the same access() check twice
hmm, if we have the fd open anyway I think a better check would be using the fd, i.e. do fstat() here
